blocks.text: Business speakers have long known the value of audiovisual (AV) aids in getting their ideas across an audience. Flip charts were the first used to emphasize points to be highlighted. However the true potential of the audiovisual medium wasn’t realized until speakers began to use electronic equipment such as overhead projectors and color slide projectors to make their picture charts, and graphs more visual; and thus more memorable.

Today business speakers must meet new performance standards set by television advertising, music videos, etc. The graphics for slides are often generated by highly sophisticated computer systems. Yesterday’s speech has become today’s presentation, accompanied by music, sound effects and multiple images flashing on giant screens.

A modern computer system that can generate slides of film strips can cost almost half of a million dollars, but most are priced between $ 5,000 and $10,000. The simple slide projector is the most common and cheapest mode of presentation. Sophisticated systems which can link several projectors in a fully synchronized sound and light presentation are available. Money invested in audio-visual equipment can pay better off in communication.

blocks.text: *Jack Brown* – President · *Henry Fischer* – Vice-President · *William Turner* – General Manager

items: *J.B.:* I’ve called this board meeting because we have to make some important decisions. Our sales have totalled Bs. 5,000,000 this year, but the profit margin has gone down because of the weakness of our currency and higher costs for raw material and labor.
*W.T.:* Sir, I haven’t been informed about this …
*J.B.:* We apologize, but all the reports were not available until Monday.
*J.B.:* Not really, our sales figures have gone up, and our long term prospects are excellent.
*W.T.:* At least, that’s good news. We will have to invest in new machinery.
*J.B.:* About Bs. 10,000,000, we’ll raise our productivity and lower our tax bill.
*W.T.:* How has the advertising campaign gone?
*H.F.:* It’s gone quite well. We’ve had several new inquiries.
*J.B.:* Please gentlemen, we have to speak about the accountant’s report.
*W.T.:* I haven’t read it in detail, but his recommendations have had good results in the past.
*H.F.:* Let’s take a vote then. All in favor… OK. William, look for the quotes for the new equipment.
*J.B.:* Let’s continue with the next point on the agenda. Stop the tape.

items.q: Why has the profit margin gone down?
What has happened to the sales figures?
What will raise the productivity and lower the tax bill?
How has the advertising campaign gone?
What have they said about the accountant’s report?
Did they agree on their vote?
What does William have to do?
